guard: a wait for the delivery daemon we launched is not answered by some OTHER daemon's ready lease (#837)
why: THE READY FLAG ANSWERS A QUESTION NOBODY ASKED. `ready:true` on the shard-0 lease means SOME
daemon bound `ctl.delivery`; the caller is asking whether THE DAEMON IT JUST STARTED did. Those
differ exactly when it matters: a SIGKILLed holder leaves its ready record for the rest of the
bucket TTL, so a replacement that lost the CAS and exited was reported ready off the corpse's
lease. The mutation restores that read, and the assertion it must redden is the one that names
a DIFFERENT holder - not the control that waits for the real one, which stays green under it.
THE TWO CONTROLS ARE PART OF THE PROOF, not decoration. Scoping the wait to a holder can fail in
the other direction - answering false for a daemon that IS ready, or refusing the ADOPTION case
where the caller genuinely cannot know the id of a daemon that was already running. Both are
asserted beside the negative, so a fix that simply never returns true does not pass this suite.
NO BUILD STEP BELONGS HERE. The suite imports `../src/index.js` relatively, so the mutated file
IS the module under test. A `completionMarker` IS declared: this suite is not fail-fast (it
counts pass/fail and prints its banner either way), so a run that dies before the banner died of
something other than the assertion named.

mutations.name: the wait accepts ANY ready lease again, as it did before #837
mutations.find: if (info.ready === true && (opts.holder === undefined || info.holder === opts.holder)) return true;
mutations.expectRed: a ready lease held by another daemon does NOT answer for the one we launched
